---
title: "Drafts: pages that are not ready yet"
---

## Overview

Drafts let you keep unfinished pages in a website project without
publishing them. By default a draft page renders as a blank page, and
nothing on the site links to it. It is left out of navigation,
listings, search, the sitemap and `llms.txt`. While you preview the
site, drafts are shown in full, with a "Draft" banner, so you can keep
working on them.

## Marking a page as a draft

Add `draft: true` to the page's front matter:

```yaml
---
title: "Post with code"
draft: true
---
```

To mark every page in a directory, put `draft: true` in that
directory's `_metadata.yml`:

```{.yaml filename="posts/_metadata.yml"}
draft: true
```

You can also list drafts by path with `drafts`, written either at the
top level or under `website:`:

```{.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
website:
  title: "Cool Website"
  drafts:
    - posts/post-with-code/index.qmd
    - "posts/wip-*.qmd"
    - scratch
```

Each entry is a path or a glob pattern. A bare directory (`scratch`)
covers everything beneath it. Like other paths in project metadata,
each entry is relative to the file it is written in: entries in
`_quarto.yml` are relative to the project root, and a leading `/`
always means the project root. A `drafts` list in `posts/_metadata.yml`
is relative to `posts/` and only applies to pages under `posts/`. An
entry that is not a path, points outside the project, or is not a
valid pattern is reported as
[Q-5-50](../../errors/project/Q-5-50.qmd) and ignored.

::: {.callout-note}
Quarto 1 also suggests keeping the list in a separate file pulled in
with `metadata-files:`. Quarto 2 does not support `metadata-files` yet,
so put the list in `_quarto.yml`, a project profile, or a
`_metadata.yml`.
:::

## How drafts appear: `draft-mode`

`draft-mode` controls what a draft looks like in the rendered site:

| `draft-mode`       | The draft page                   | Links to it    |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `gone` (default)   | blank                            | removed        |
| `unlinked`         | rendered, with a "Draft" banner  | removed        |
| `visible`          | rendered, with a "Draft" banner  | kept           |

```{.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
website:
  draft-mode: unlinked
```

When links to a draft are removed:

- Navbar, sidebar and page-footer entries for the page are dropped. A
  sidebar section whose heading links to the draft keeps its other
  entries and just loses the link.
- A link to the draft in another page's text keeps its text but loses
  the link.
- The page is left out of listings and their RSS feeds, site search,
  `sitemap.xml`, and `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt`.

A `gone` draft still has a URL: Quarto writes a blank page there, so
anyone who already has the link sees an empty page instead of a 404.
The blank page is marked `noindex`, so search engines that find it do
not index it.

### Setting `draft-mode` for part of a site

`draft-mode` is ordinary metadata, so it can be set anywhere metadata
can: `_quarto.yml`, a directory's `_metadata.yml`, a page's front
matter, or `--metadata` on the command line. Each draft follows the
value that applies to it. For example, to show draft blog posts with a
banner while every other draft stays `gone`:

```{.yaml filename="posts/_metadata.yml"}
draft-mode: unlinked
```

You can write it as `draft-mode` or as `website: draft-mode:`. If you
use both spellings in different files, the top-level `draft-mode`
always wins over `website: draft-mode`, even when the `website:` one
is in a more specific file such as a `_metadata.yml`. Using one
spelling everywhere avoids surprises. An unrecognized value is
reported as [Q-5-49](../../errors/project/Q-5-49.qmd), and the draft is
treated as `gone`.

## Previewing drafts

Whatever `draft-mode` says, drafts are always shown in full when you
preview: in the browser preview, in `q2 preview --static`, and in
downloads and exports made from the preview. Draft pages show the
"Draft" banner, and links and navigation entries pointing at them work
normally. `draft-mode` applies only to the site you render with
`q2 render` and publish.

## Drafts and aliases

A draft writes no [alias](aliases.qmd) redirects, whatever its
`draft-mode`.

## Outside websites

`draft-mode` and blank pages are website features. In other project
types, and for a single document, a draft renders in full with the
"Draft" banner. `gone` behaves like `unlinked` there.

## Differences from Quarto 1

- `drafts` entries are glob patterns and resolve relative to the file
  they are written in. Quarto 1 only matches exact project-relative
  paths.
- `draft-mode` can be set per directory or per page. Quarto 1 reads a
  single site-wide value.
- Previews always show drafts. In Quarto 1, an explicit
  `draft-mode: gone` also blanked pages in preview.
- A `gone` page is marked `noindex`.
- A sidebar section whose heading links to a draft keeps its other
  entries. Quarto 1 drops the whole section.
